newsitem.title: LATVIA: Hansapank Latvia unit to boost capital.
newsitem.headline: Hansapank Latvia unit to boost capital.

text.p: Hansabank-Latvija, the Latvian subsidiary of Estonia's Hansapank, the largest bank in the Baltic states, said on Tuesday it would apply for permission to boost its share capital by one million lats.
It also said it had an oral agreement with an international financial institution for an injection of two to four million dollars in subordinated capital in the second quarter of 1997.
"The management board of Hansabank-Latvija will apply to the Bank of Latvia (the central bank) with a request to increase the bank's share capital by one million lats," it said in a statement.
It said that two tranches, each worth 500,000 lats, were planned. The first would be issued by the end of December, the second during the first quarter of next year.
Hansabank-Latvija currently has 2.1 million lats in registered share capital.

Hansapank yesterday said that after revising provisions for loan losses, Hansabank-Latvija made a loss of 12.46 million Estonian kroons in the first nine months of the year versus an earlier estimate of a 1.33 million kroon profit.
Hansabank bought the Latvian bank, formerly called Deutsche Lettische Bank, in June, making it the first cross-border bank merger in the Baltic states.
